# `js/filename-case`

**File and folder names in one case (kebab case by default)**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:js/strict` at `error` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `case`, `cases`, `ignore`, `checkDirectories`, `directoryRoots`, `multipleFileExtensions` |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (renaming a file changes every import of it) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.0 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-unicorn/filename-case` |

## What it checks

A file's name (before its first `.`) and, by default, each folder on its path from the project root are in the chosen case — kebab case unless `case` or `cases` says otherwise — and the extension is lower case. Leading underscores, characters outside letters, digits, `-` and `_`, names starting with `$`, and `index.js`/`index.ts`/… are left as they are. The finding names the renamed file or folder. It is reported at the start of the file.

**Why:** One naming scheme makes files easy to find and avoids imports that work on one file system and fail on a case-sensitive one.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:js/strict` sets it to `error`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/strict"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/filename-case" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `case` | `string` | `"kebabCase"` | kebabCase, camelCase, snakeCase or pascalCase |
| `cases` | `object` | `{}` | several cases allowed at once, as { kebabCase: true, pascalCase: true }; wins over case |
| `ignore` | `string[]` | `[]` | regular expressions: a path segment that matches one is not checked |
| `checkDirectories` | `boolean` | `true` | check the folder names on the file's path too |
| `directoryRoots` | `string[]` | `[]` | folders (a path or a regular expression) below which folder names are checked |
| `multipleFileExtensions` | `boolean` | `true` | treat everything after the first dot as the extension (`a.test.js`) |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."js/filename-case"]
severity = "error"

[rules."js/filename-case".options]
case = "kebabCase"
cases = {}
ignore = []
checkDirectories = true
directoryRoots = []
multipleFileExtensions = true
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"js/filename-case" = { severity = "error", options = { case = "pascalCase", cases = {}, ignore = ["<name>"], checkDirectories = false, directoryRoots = ["<name>"], multipleFileExtensions = false } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `case`

*string* · default `"kebabCase"`

kebabCase, camelCase, snakeCase or pascalCase

```toml
[rules."js/filename-case".options]
case = "pascalCase"
```

#### `cases`

*object* · default `{}`

several cases allowed at once, as { kebabCase: true, pascalCase: true }; wins over case

```toml
[rules."js/filename-case".options]
cases = {}
```

#### `ignore`

*string[]* · default `[]`

regular expressions: a path segment that matches one is not checked

```toml
[rules."js/filename-case".options]
ignore = ["<name>"]
```

#### `checkDirectories`

*boolean* · default `true`

check the folder names on the file's path too

```toml
[rules."js/filename-case".options]
checkDirectories = false
```

#### `directoryRoots`

*string[]* · default `[]`

folders (a path or a regular expression) below which folder names are checked

```toml
[rules."js/filename-case".options]
directoryRoots = ["<name>"]
```

#### `multipleFileExtensions`

*boolean* · default `true`

treat everything after the first dot as the extension (`a.test.js`)

```toml
[rules."js/filename-case".options]
multipleFileExtensions = false
```

### Options in action

Each case below is one of the rule's tests (`packs/js/rules/js/filename-case.cases.md`): the options, the input, and what codelaw reports.

#### pascal case allowed

```toml
[rules."js/filename-case".options]
case = "pascalCase"
checkDirectories = false
```

*As the file* `src/MyUtils.js`:

```js
export const x = 1;
```

**Reports nothing.**

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/filename-case" = { options = { case = "pascalCase" } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/filename-case" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/filename-case" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/filename-case" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/filename-case" = { severity = "warn", options = { case = "pascalCase" } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/filename-case": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"case": "pascalCase"}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/filename-case: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/filename-case expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/filename-case --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/filename-case       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/filename-case  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>    # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Rename the file (or folder) to the name the message gives, and update its imports.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js path=src/MyUtils.js
export const x = 1;
```

#### Do

```js path=src/my-utils.js
export const x = 1;
```

### JSX

#### Don't

```jsx path=src/MyUtils.jsx
export const x = 1;
```

#### Do

```jsx path=src/my-utils.jsx
export const x = 1;
```

### TypeScript

#### Don't

```ts path=src/MyUtils.ts
export const x = 1;
```

#### Do

```ts path=src/my-utils.ts
export const x = 1;
```

### TSX

#### Don't

```tsx path=src/MyUtils.tsx
export const x = 1;
```

#### Do

```tsx path=src/my-utils.tsx
export const x = 1;
```
